historical_growth.growth_rate_source: mid_cycle_revenue_cagr (NOT a historical CAGR -- the historical revenue/equity/FCF CAGRs above are gold-price-cycle and Kiaka-construction-ramp artefacts and are explicitly not used to drive the projection). 5.0% is the CAGR IMPLIED by this build's own bottom-up mid-cycle revenue path (FY2025 A$1,543m -> 2035 A$2,521m at a normalized US,200/oz gold price and the 10-year production target), reported here only so cross-ticker PEG screens have a forward-growth proxy that is not a peak-price artefact. See inputs.notes for the full construction.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (59.8%) diverges >30% from revenue 5yr CAGR (37.7%) and FCF 5yr CAGR (57.5%) diverges from both -- entirely explained by the FY2020-2025 gold price roughly tripling combined with the Kiaka construction-to-production transition (FY2023-24 FCF was structurally negative funding Kiaka capex, then swung sharply positive from FY2025). Not a data quality issue; not used as the growth driver regardless.

scenario_narratives.base: Two-mine steady-state producer at guided/targeted physical volumes and a normalized mid-cycle gold price; the Kiaka government stake increase to 40% completes on the announced paid (not expropriated) terms and no further BF demands materialize.
scenario_narratives.bull: Higher-for-longer gold price, faster Kiaka ramp to the top of the 10-year target range, and the Kiaka stake dilution proves to be the final BF ask rather than a template for further demands.
scenario_narratives.bear: Gold price reverts sharply from the current cycle peak, Kiaka execution risk recurs, and Burkina Faso's resource-nationalism pattern extends beyond Kiaka to Sanbrado/Toega or is mirrored elsewhere in the group.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Mid-cycle owner-FCF component DCF. WAF has completed its transition from single-mine cash generator (funding Kiaka construction, FCF negative FY2023-24) to a two-mine steady-state producer (Sanbrado mature since 2020, Kiaka in operations since August 2025), so a risked pre-revenue NPV model is no longer appropriate -- but FY2025 and especially H1 2026 sit at a gold-price-cycle peak (realised US$3,525/oz and US$4,744/oz against a 5-years-ago spot near US$1,780/oz and current spot ~US$4,308/oz) that must not be naively annualized or extrapolated. The model separates the two things that are actually happening: (1) a REAL, disclosed operating ramp -- Kiaka's first full year of production, the 10-year target averaging 533,000oz/yr -- captured directly as physical ounces; and (2) a CYCLICAL gold-price input, normalized to a mid-cycle US$3,200/oz (a real haircut off both spot and the recent realised prices) rather than carried forward from the peak. Burkina Faso jurisdictional risk (military government since 2022, an active insurgency, a 2025 trading suspension, and a completed pattern of forced-but-paid equity dilution at Kiaka) is charged once, in the discount rate (+4.5pp WACC premium) and via a materially elevated bear-case probability weight (30%, vs the house default 15%) -- not doubled up in the flows. The Kiaka government stake increase (WAF's interest 85%->60%) is modelled explicitly as a step-up in the combined tax+NCI leakage rate from ~29% (FY2025 actual, pre-increase) to ~53% (post-transaction, calibrated to tie almost exactly to H1 2026's actual pre-transaction leakage of 48.6%), which is the single largest driver of the gap between this valuation and a naive extrapolation of recent reported profit.
key_risks_to_valuation: Gold price: the entire model is a bet that US$3,200/oz is a reasonable mid-cycle anchor -- if gold instead holds near the current US$4,300+/oz spot or the H1 2026 realised US$4,744/oz indefinitely, this valuation understates fair value materially; if gold reverts toward pre-2024 levels (sub-US$2,500/oz), it overstates it

Further Burkina Faso resource-nationalism beyond the announced Kiaka SA stake increase -- a similar demand at Sanbrado or Toega is not modelled in the base case beyond the bear-scenario probability weight
Kiaka ramp execution -- the 2026 explosives-permit issue shows operational/permitting risk persists even post-construction
Royalty regime escalation is now uncapped and price-linked; a further increase in the escalation schedule is a downside not separately modelled
AUD/USD assumption (0.66 long-run vs H1 2026's actual 0.70) -- a structurally weaker AUD would lift AUD-denominated revenue/margins beyond this model

band_position in the generated DCF JSON reads -1514.3, an engine artefact: SBC is ~0.4% of revenue here (effectively an SBC-near-zero market per adaptations section 7e), so house (A$4.60) and street (A$4.67) intrinsic values differ by only A$0.07 -- the engine's 1%-of-IV threshold for collapsing the band to null is not quite met by this small absolute gap, producing a large but meaningless ratio. Read band_position as n/a, not as a real reading of where price sits in an SBC-driven band; house and street values themselves (A$4.60 vs A$4.67) are the correct pair to compare.

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report cash flow statement (share-based payments add-back A$6.1m; no separate equity-award-tax withholding line disclosed)
inputs.wacc_rationale: AUD-denominated flows discounted at an AUD-built WACC: ~9.0% base ASX industrial rate (AU 10yr risk-free ~4.2%, ERP ~5.5%, modest beta) plus a +4.5pp Burkina Faso jurisdictional risk premium (military government since the 2022 coup, active regional insurgency, an Aug-Nov 2025 ASX trading suspension triggered by a government equity-stake demand, and an uncapped/escalating gold royalty regime) = 13.5%. This premium is charged in the discount rate, not stacked again in the flows or via a higher bear-case WACC (adaptations section 7f, charge risk once); gold-price cyclicality is instead handled by normalizing the flows to a mid-cycle price rather than extrapolating the FY2025/H1 2026 peak.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A), leases as debt: lease liabilities (A$23.1m at 30 June 2026: A$11.0m current + A$12.1m non-current) folded into net_debt; lease principal/interest is NOT separately deducted from the flows because the flows are built bottom-up from production x mid-cycle price x cash-cost components (not from reported OCF/FCF), so there is no reported-FCF base in which a lease payment could be double-counted. Immaterial in scale either way (<1% of EV).
inputs.nci_treatment: Attributable-only flows via a combined tax+NCI leakage rate in cash_tax_rate_path (adaptations 7c). Burkina Faso free-carry is 15% across Sanbrado/Toega and Kiaka SA (unaffected by the 2026 Kiaka transaction), but the government's April 2026 decree raises its PAID stake in Kiaka SA specifically from 15% to 40% (WAF's Kiaka SA interest 85% -> 60%), completing by end of CY2026. Modelled as a blended group NCI rate = 42% x 15% (Sanbrado/Toega, ~42% of segment profit) + 58% x NCI_kiaka (~58% of segment profit, in line with H1 2026's 62.7% Kiaka segment-result share, held slightly below that as Sanbrado/Toega mature). NCI_kiaka is held at the pre-transaction 15% blended two-thirds of the way through 2026 (transaction completing only 'by end of calendar 2026') then steps to the post-transaction 40% from 2027 onward. Combined with the 30% Burkina Faso statutory corporate tax rate (1-(1-tax)(1-NCI)) plus a 2-5pp tapering allowance for withholding tax on intercompany dividend repatriation (A$118m higher other-expenses in H1 2026 from this as profits/repatriation increased -- some transitional, some likely recurring as cash continues moving up from the BF subsidiaries), this is the cash_tax_rate_path. Calibration: modelled 2026 combined leakage 48.5% vs H1 2026 ACTUAL (still pre-transaction) of 48.6% -- ties almost exactly. FY2025 actual combined leakage was 28.6%, before the royalty/withholding spike and before the Kiaka stake increase; the path is explicitly NOT held at that lower historical level.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, mid-cycle component build (routed via .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md to the cyclical/non-US owner-FCF row + adaptations). WAF is now a steady two-mine producer (Sanbrado mature since 2020, Kiaka in operations since Aug 2025), not pre-revenue, so a risked-NPV project-finance model is no longer the right tool -- but FY2025 and H1 2026 both sit at or near a gold-price-cycle peak (realised US$3,525/oz and US$4,744/oz respectively, against 5yr-ago prices near US$1,780/oz spot and a current spot of ~US$4,308/oz) and must not be naively extrapolated. Revenue is built bottom-up as guided/targeted PHYSICAL production (2026 guidance midpoint 460,000oz; 10-year target averaging 533,000oz/yr 2026-2035, peaking 596,000oz in 2030 -- both real, disclosed operating plans) multiplied by a NORMALIZED mid-cycle gold price of US$3,200/oz (a ~33% haircut off current spot US$4,308/oz and well below the FY2025/H1 2026 realised prices, while still well above the pre-2022 base, reflecting gold's structural re-rating without extrapolating the peak) at a long-run AUD/USD of 0.66 (vs H1 2026's actual 0.70, itself a partial contributor to the AUD-price peak). EBITDA margin is built bottom-up from Adjusted Operating Cost components disclosed in the H1 2026 cost-per-ounce table (mining+processing+admin cash cost ex-royalty, and the price-linked Burkina Faso royalty computed at the mid-cycle price's own royalty band, not carried forward from the peak-price actual) -- cross-checked against FY2024's actual 55.2% EBITDA margin (at a much lower US$2,391/oz realised price and lower Kiaka-free AISC), landing at a comparable but appropriately higher 58-62% band given gold's structurally higher price level. Historical revenue/equity/FCF CAGRs (37-75%) are gold-price-cycle and Kiaka-construction-ramp artefacts and are explicitly NOT used to drive the projection; they are reported in historical_growth for the record only. Both interest income (A$9.1m FY2025) and SBC (A$6.1m FY2025) are immaterial relative to the FCF base (<3%) but still stripped/expensed per the method's standard rule. Share count held flat (SBC is fully expensed in the flows); no buybacks to date.

bear.narrative: Gold price reverts hard toward US$2,200/oz (still above 2023 levels but well off the 2025-26 peak) as real rates rise and safe-haven demand fades, compressing margins across both unhedged mines simultaneously. Kiaka's explosives-permit-style execution issues recur and delay the ramp to nameplate. Burkina Faso's demonstrated willingness to compel additional equity (Kiaka SA 15% to 40%) extends to a further demand at Sanbrado or Toega, or a similar move by extension of the precedent; the royalty regime tightens further. WACC rises 2pp reflecting the crystallised pattern of resource-nationalism risk.

base.narrative: Sanbrado (mature, ~15% BF free-carry) and Kiaka (ramping to full nameplate through 2026-2027, BF stake rising from 15% to a paid 40% by end-2026) both run at guided/targeted physical production -- 2026 guidance midpoint 460,000oz group, 10-year target averaging 533,000oz/yr peaking 596,000oz in 2030 -- multiplied by a normalized mid-cycle gold price of US$3,200/oz (a real haircut off both current spot ~US$4,308/oz and the FY2025/H1 2026 realised prices). Margins settle around 58-62% as Kiaka's ramp-up cost premium fades and owner-mining efficiencies land, cross-checked against FY2024's actual 55.2% margin at a much lower gold price. Cash tax + NCI leakage steps up sharply from FY2025's actual 28.6% to ~53% once the Kiaka government stake increase completes and the royalty regime's price-linked escalation is reflected at the mid-cycle price -- calibrated to tie to H1 2026's actual 48.6% pre-transaction leakage.

bull.narrative: Gold price stays structurally elevated (mid-cycle US$3,800/oz, less mean reversion than base) as central-bank buying and geopolitical demand persist; Kiaka and Sanbrado/Toega both hit the high end of the 10-year target (620,000oz peak) with fewer permitting hiccups; the Kiaka stake dilution to 40% resolves as the final BF ask with no further demands at Sanbrado/Toega or from other jurisdictions; owner-mining and scale efficiencies bring costs down faster than base. WACC eases 1.5pp on the BF relationship de-risking demonstrated by the paid (not expropriated) Kiaka transaction.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 10x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear weight raised from the house default 15% to 30%: WAF carries a demonstrated (not hypothetical) jurisdictional risk -- an actual 3-month ASX trading suspension in 2025 triggered by a Burkina Faso government equity demand, a military government in power since a 2022 coup with an active regional insurgency, an uncapped and price-escalating royalty regime, and a completed precedent (Kiaka SA free-carry 15%->40%) that could plausibly extend to Sanbrado/Toega. Bull weight trimmed to 25% because the bull case requires BOTH a higher-for-longer gold price AND a clean resolution of BF risk with no further demands -- two largely independent conditions both needing to hold. Base takes the remaining 45%.
